category_title: High-achieving students who dominate group work and exclude peers in competitive settings
student_description: This high-achieving student dominates group work, demeans slower peers, and takes over decision-making, especially on multiple-choice tasks where they can dictate the 'right' answer. They uniquely require open-ended, discovery-based tasks without a single correct answer, structured division of labor, and peer assessment to force genuine cooperation and interpersonal accountability.

criteria.criterion_name: Task Interdependence via Division of Labor
criteria.rationale: Dividing a project into distinct parts ensures every group member has a mandatory contribution, preventing the high-achieving student from doing all the work themselves.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include structuring group projects so that responsibilities are explicitly divided into smaller parts assigned to individual members.

criteria.rationale: Incorporating peer assessment holds the student accountable for their interpersonal behavior and incentivizes them to assist rather than demean slower teammates.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate peer assessment as a formal component of the student's evaluation or grading.

criteria.rationale: Working towards a comprehensive joint product forces the student to synthesize the divided parts and share intellectual resources with their peers.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must require the group to combine their individual contributions into a single, comprehensive joint product or presentation.
